1: Nehemiah, cupbearer to the Persian king, hears that Jerusalem's walls are in ruins. He weeps, fasts and prays.
Concern for God's people begins in prayer.
2: The king notices his sadness. Nehemiah prays quickly and asks leave to rebuild. He inspects the walls by night.
A short silent prayer before a hard conversation.
3: A list of who repaired each section of the wall: priests, goldsmiths, merchants, and one man with his daughters.
Everyone builds the part in front of their own house.
4: Enemies mock and plot an attack. Nehemiah posts guards, and the builders work with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other.
"We prayed to our God and set a guard." Prayer and prudence together.
5: The poor complain that rich Jews are charging interest and taking their children as slaves. Nehemiah makes them give it all back, and refuses his own governor's allowance.
Rebuilding walls is pointless if the people inside exploit each other.
6: Enemies try to lure Nehemiah away and to frighten him. He replies, "I am doing a great work and cannot come down." The wall is finished in fifty-two days.
7: Nehemiah appoints guards and finds the record of the first returnees.
The city needs people as well as walls.
8: Ezra reads the law aloud from dawn to noon while Levites explain it. The people weep, and are told, "The joy of the Lord is your strength."
Scripture read and explained to the assembly: the pattern of the Liturgy of the Word.
9: The people fast and the Levites pray through Israel's whole history: God's constant mercy and their constant rebellion.
"You are a God ready to forgive."
10: Leaders put their names to a written promise to keep the law, the Sabbath and the support of the Temple.
11: One family in ten is chosen by lot to live in the city, and others volunteer.
Some give up comfort for the common good.
12: After lists of priests, two great choirs walk the wall in opposite directions and meet at the Temple. The joy is heard far away.
13: Returning after an absence, Nehemiah finds the Temple misused, the Sabbath broken and mixed marriages again. He puts things right.
